answer: The cheapest real defence: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because jetty only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
